output.summary: KEP-4222 proposes CBOR as an alternative wire format for Kubernetes API clients and servers, and as the storage serialization for custom resources in apiextensions-apiserver, replacing JSON there. Its status is implementable at stage beta.
output.rationale: Custom resources cannot use Protobuf, which needs code generation and compile-time schemas, so high-volume custom resources pay JSON codec costs on every request hop. The readme cites benchmarks of up to roughly 8x faster custom resource encode/decode and 2x faster dynamic client decode, from CBOR as a self-describing binary format. The stated goal is to cut CPU and heap churn where Protobuf cannot be used, while not replacing Protobuf or all JSON/YAML.

alternatives.option: Keep JSON as the only serialization for custom resources
alternatives.why_not: The readme says custom resources are at a serious efficiency disadvantage versus native resources, and benchmarks suggest CBOR reduces that cost. The sources do not record a reason this option was rejected.

alternatives.option: Use a Kubernetes-specific length-prefixed CBOR framing scheme
alternatives.why_not: A reviewer (benluddy) said it would be preferable to adopt the standardized CBOR Sequences scheme rather than a Kubernetes-specific framing, though length-prefixed framing may perform better. The sources do not show a final framing decision.

alternatives.option: Two separate feature gates, one for storage and one for serving
alternatives.why_not: Suggested by sftim. jpbetz preferred a single gate that stops storing and serving CBOR but still reads it from storage, so turning it off is safe. The sources do not show a final decision.

evidence.quote: It will supersede JSON in apiextensions-apiserver for storage serialization of custom resources.
Benchmarks suggest that custom resource and dynamic client encode and decode operations can be made up to approximately 8x and 2x faster
Replace existing usage of Protobuf. - Substantially reduce the size of encoded objects (a modest size reduction is anticipated).
it would be preferable to adopt that scheme vs. defining a CBOR framing scheme that is Kubernetes-specific.
I'm onboard with a single feature gate where we stop storing an serving CBOR, but continue to support reading it from storage.
